claims.text: The target materials are nanoparticles containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially crystallized as a single-phase solid solution.
Local lattice distortions generate a rough energy landscape in multimetal nanoparticles.
A rough energy landscape produced by lattice distortion impedes atomic diffusion.
The extent to which lattice distortion impedes diffusion governs the maintenance of single-phase structural and chemical stability.
Sufficiently high lattice distortion and diffusion barriers mitigate phase separation.
Sufficiently high lattice distortion and diffusion barriers mitigate grain growth.
Sufficiently high lattice distortion and diffusion barriers mitigate chemical segregation at temperatures as high as 1923 K.
Changing elemental radius mismatch while retaining equiatomic ratios can vary the magnitude of local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions and grain-boundary characteristics slow atomic diffusion.
Slower atomic diffusion suppresses phase separation.
Configurational entropy combined with lattice distortion creates a rough energy landscape.
Limiting atomic mobility inhibits coarsening, chemical segregation, and precipitation.
Enthalpic driving forces for phase separation can overcome diffusion barriers at extreme temperatures or under reactive catalytic conditions.
Higher-distortion nanoparticles will retain a single-phase structure better than lower-distortion nanoparticles during exposure from 473 to 1923 K.
Higher-distortion nanoparticles will retain a more uniform chemical distribution than lower-distortion nanoparticles during thermal exposure.
Lower-distortion nanoparticles may exhibit phase separation, grain coarsening, or segregation over time between 473 and 1923 K.
Bulk diffusion dominates over surface diffusion in sufficiently large particles.
Extremely small particles or strongly reactive environments may deviate from the predicted distortion-stability relationship.
The hypothesis is falsified if the nominally higher-distortion particles show similar or greater phase separation, grain growth, or chemical segregation than the lower-distortion particles.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes changing elemental radius differences, which ordinarily requires changing elemental identities or fractions, whereas the experiment requires the two sets to have identical overall compositions. No alternative method, such as controlled strain, ordering, or defect content, is specified for producing different intrinsic lattice distortions at identical composition.
